proofs.proof_tex:
The face-robust tangent-score lemma proves from the positivity premise that every conditional vector
\(p_{n,x,h,\zeta}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\) is a probability distribution and proves that its count target is the exact finite-population contrast.  Conditional on the three coordinates, drawing a multinomial count and then choosing a labeling uniformly in its orbit is equivalent to drawing the labeled response types independently.  Indeed, for a labeled type sequence with count vector \(m\), the product of its multinomial mass and the reciprocal orbit size is
\[
\left\{\frac{n!}{\prod_tm_t!}\prod_t
(p_{n,x,h,\zeta,t}^{\dagger,\mathrm A})^{m_t}\right\}
\left\{\frac{\prod_tm_t!}{n!}\right\}
=\prod_{i=1}^np_{n,x,h,\zeta,t_i}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}.
\tag{1}
\]

Fix an assignment vector \(a_0\) with count vector \(r\).  Given a response-count vector \(m\), the prior is uniform over all labeled type sequences in that orbit.  Counting the type-by-arm tables compatible with the observed arm-success vector gives exactly
\(P_m(X^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid r)\) from the orbit-likelihood definition.  Two labeled outcome vectors with the same arm-success counts differ by a permutation within assigned-arm blocks.  Both the prior and the exact target are invariant under that permutation.  Therefore the posterior distribution of the target depends on the labeled observations only through \((r,X^{\mathrm{obs}})\).

For any action \(d\), conditional square completion gives
\[
\mathbb E\{(d-\tau)^2\mid r,X^{\mathrm{obs}}\}
=\operatorname{Var}(\tau\mid r,X^{\mathrm{obs}})
+\{d-\mathbb E(\tau\mid r,X^{\mathrm{obs}})\}^2.
\tag{2}
\]
The identity remains valid after averaging estimator randomization.  Thus the posterior mean minimizes conditional squared error, and summing its posterior variance with the exact likelihood gives
\(\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\) by the exact Airy-tube Bayes-risk definition.

Now let \(A\sim\mathcal D_n\).  Outcome independence ensures that conditioning on an assignment vector does not change the schedule prior.  Any two assignment vectors with the same count are related by a common unit permutation, so the minimum conditional Bayes risk is the same and equals the fixed-count value above.  Applying (2) conditionally on every assignment vector and grouping by the induced count law \(\pi\) gives the first inequality in the statement.  Its right side is a convex average of the fixed-count risks and is therefore at least their minimum
\(B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\).  This proves the claim for arbitrary dependence across assignments and arbitrary randomized labeled-data estimators.

The face-robust tangent-score lemma and the positivity premise make every response vector in the prior a probability distribution.  On each rational spline piece and each of the eight sign cells, the integrand defining a response-count weight is a product of the rational polynomials
\(w_k^\dagger\), \(\rho_\varepsilon\), and \(\rho_\varepsilon\) with integer powers of affine polynomials in \(\alpha_n\).  Exact iterated integration therefore gives
\[
\nu_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(m)
\in\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)
\qquad(m\in\mathcal M_{n,3}).
\tag{1}
\]
The orbit likelihood and finite-population target are rational by the exact-primitives proposition.  Hence every posterior denominator, numerator, positive-denominator quotient, fixed-count Bayes risk, and scaled deficit belongs to
\(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\).  All indexing sets are finite:
\[
|\mathcal M_{n,3}|<\infty,
\quad |\mathcal R_{n,3}|<\infty,
\quad \prod_{a=1}^3(r_a+1)<\infty,
\quad |\mathcal H(m,r,x^{\mathrm{obs}})|<\infty.
\tag{2}
\]

Represent an element of \(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\) by a rational polynomial evaluated at the isolated positive root of \(nX^3-1\), reducing modulo that root's square-free polynomial.  Rational polynomial remainder sequences isolate the real roots of every numerator.  Refining the isolating interval for \(\alpha_n\) decides its sign unless the reduced numerator is identically zero, which its rational coefficients decide directly.  Thus every branch, comparison, and finite minimum or maximum in (1)--(2) terminates.  Rational bisection of the selected Bayes value inside \([0,1]\) terminates with endpoints of width at most \(\delta\).

The face-robust orbit-Bayes lemma gives, for every admissible outcome-independent design and labeled estimator, Bayes risk at least
\[
B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
=\min_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r).
\tag{3}
\]
Maximum risk dominates Bayes risk.  Taking the infimum in the risk-game definition and using the returned lower endpoint yields
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)\ge
B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\ge b^-.
\tag{4}
\]

For the attaining side, the observation alphabet, action grid, and schedule set in the evaluator definition are finite.  Under rational
\(q^\dagger\), every coefficient
\(P_y(\omega)\{a_j-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\) is rational.  Enumeration of finitely many rational basic feasible solutions therefore returns a feasible optimizer \((z,U)\).  The simplex constraints make \(z\) a Markov kernel into \([-1,1]\), hence a total randomized estimator.  Its constraints give risk at most \(U\) for every fixed schedule.  This design is feasible in the risk game, so
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)\le U.
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (1)--(5) prove every same-input claim and make no cross-sample assertion.

The exact-primitives proposition gives
\[
\kappa(c^\dagger)=\frac58.
\tag{1}
\]
The Airy-benchmark definition and \(C_A\in(0,\infty)\) therefore give
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A\kappa(c^\dagger)^{2/3}
=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\in(0,\infty).
\tag{2}
\]
Fix \(n\) in the admissible tail of the allocation-tube theorem.  Its positivity certificate is
\[
\alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+4\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A})\le1.
\tag{3}
\]
The face-robust orbit-Bayes lemma applies.  Since maximum risk dominates Bayes risk, taking the infimum over exactly the designs and estimators in the risk-game definition gives
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)
\ge B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}.
\tag{4}
\]
This compares risks for the exact finite-population target, because the tangent-score lemma and the exact-primitives proposition retain
\(\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)=n^{-1}\sum_tm_t(c^\dagger)^\top t\).

The exact Bayes-risk definition and finiteness of \(\mathcal R_{n,3}\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
n^{4/3}\left\{\frac1n-
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\right\}
&=n^{4/3}\left\{\frac1n-
\min_r\mathcal B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\right\}\\
&=\max_rG_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r).
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
The three allocation sets in conclusion (A) partition \(\mathcal R_{n,3}\).  Applying the corresponding line of (A) to each member and using (5) gives
\[
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
\ge\frac1n-\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-\}n^{-4/3}.
\tag{6}
\]
Equations (4) and (6) prove the first two inequalities in (1).

Conclusion (B) supplies the displayed total procedure and its upper risk bound.  Its design and estimator are feasible in the risk game, so the minimax infimum is no larger than its maximum risk.  This proves the last two inequalities in (1).  Subtracting the resulting risk bounds from \(n^{-1}\) and multiplying by \(n^{4/3}>0\) gives
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-.
\tag{7}
\]
Conclusion (C) bounds each error in (7) by \(E(N)\) for every \(n\ge N\), proving (2).  Since \(E(N)\to0\), (7) yields convergence of the scaled deficit to \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\).  Rearrangement and (2) give the claimed expansion and strict positivity.  This is a corollary of conclusions (A)--(C); it does not supply their still-required proof.

Fix an admissible tail input \(n\).  The allocation-tube theorem and the evaluator definition give
\[
\alpha_n\{3T_{k_n}^\dagger+4\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\}\le1.
\tag{1}
\]
The effective Airy-record lemma makes the selected record a finite rational-interval object.  Applying the face-robust fixed-input evaluator with
\(\delta_n=n^{-3}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
b_n^-&\le B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
\le b_n^+,\\
b_n^+-b_n^-&\le n^{-3},\\
b_n^-&\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le
\max_y\mathbb E\!\left[
\{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\right]
\le U_n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
The lower inequality is valid against every procedure by the face-robust orbit-Bayes lemma, and the upper inequality is witnessed by the returned total estimator.

By the exact Bayes-risk definition,
\[
n^{4/3}\left\{n^{-1}-
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\right\}
=\max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r).
\tag{3}
\]
The three allocation regions in conclusion (A) partition the finite count simplex.  Hence (A) and (3) give
\[
n^{4/3}\left\{n^{-1}-
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\right\}
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-.
\tag{4}
\]
Together with (2), this yields
\(D_n\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-\) and
\(D_n\le d_n^+\).

The enclosure width in (2) gives
\[
0\le B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}-b_n^-
\le n^{-3}.
\tag{5}
\]
Using (4)--(5),
\[
d_n^+
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-+n^{4/3}n^{-3}
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-+n^{-1}.
\tag{6}
\]
Let \(U_{\Lambda,n}\) be the rational upper Airy endpoint in the verified record.  By the evaluator definition,
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\le U_{\Lambda,n},
\qquad
\left[n^{4/3}(U_n-n^{-1})+U_{\Lambda,n}\right]_+
\le e_{\mathrm{pr},n}.
\tag{7}
\]
Since \(z\le[z]_+\), equation (7) rearranges to
\[
d_n^-=n^{4/3}(n^{-1}-U_n)
\ge\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}.
\tag{8}
\]
The inequality \(R_n(c^\dagger)\le U_n\) in (2) gives
\(d_n^-\le D_n\).  Equations (4), (6), and (8) prove all finite-sample chains.

Conclusion (C) supplies a rational-valued nonincreasing computable function
\(E\) with certified convergence to zero and with every error at most \(E(N)\) for all \(n\ge N\).  Put \(F(N)=E(N)+1/N\).  Given rational
\(\eta>0\), enumerate integers \(N\) until the certificate verifies
\[
F(N)\le\eta.
\tag{9}
\]
Certified convergence makes this search terminate.  Equations (4), (6), and (8), with the tail bounds from (C), then give the enclosing relation and all three absolute-error inequalities for every later \(n\).

Diagonal mode is total by construction.  On its finite inadmissible prefix, the zero estimator has squared error at most one because the normalized contrast puts the exact target in \([-1,1]\); nonnegativity gives the opposite endpoint.  Every computation uses integer, rational, or ordered-algebraic data for the fixed rational contrast.  Thus no representation of an arbitrary real contrast is used.  As with the sharp-limit corollary, the cross-sample conclusion is inherited from (A)--(C), not proved independently here.

added_lemmas.statement:
The face-robust signed directions have zero total mass and satisfy, for both signs,
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
&\sum_t s_t&\sum_t s_tb_t&\sum_t s_t\theta_t\\ \hline
s_x^\pm&0&v&1\\
s_h^\pm&0&d^\dagger&0\\
\gamma_0&0&\mathbf1&0.
\end{array}
\]
Consequently, whenever
\(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\le1\),
\(p_{n,x,h,\zeta}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\) is a probability distribution and
\[
\mathbb E[b_t\mid x,h,\zeta]
=\alpha_n(xv+hd^\dagger+\zeta\mathbf1),
\qquad
\mathbb E[\theta_t\mid x,h,\zeta]=\alpha_nx.
\]
For every open-simplex allocation \(q\),
\[
(c^\dagger)^\top z(q)=1,
\qquad
\sum_aq_az_a(q)^2=H(q)^{-1},
\qquad
|\beta(q)|\le4,
\qquad
|\gamma(q)|\le\frac12.
\]
At \(q=q^\dagger\), \(H(q)=4\), \(z(q)=v\), and
\(\beta(q)=\gamma(q)=0\).  The local directional energy at this allocation is certified by
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\le
J_x(k)+\frac58\int_{\mathbb R}|x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+2^{-k},
\]
so the face guards add no local score cost and the coefficient converges to
\(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\).  If arm \(j\) is absent, the direction with arm-marginal derivative \(e_j/c_j^\dagger\) has parameter coordinates
\[
(1,0,1/2),\qquad (1,-4,-1/2),\qquad
(1,4/3,-1/2)
\]
for \(j=1,2,3\), respectively; hence every single-arm or two-arm proper face has a target derivative-one direction whose revealed arm marginals have derivative zero.

For the product density
\(w_k^\dagger(x)\rho_\varepsilon(h)\rho_\varepsilon(\zeta)\), directional integration by parts in
\(D_{\beta,\gamma}=\partial_x+\beta\partial_h+\gamma\partial_\zeta\) has no boundary term and its prior score \(S_{\beta,\gamma}\) satisfies
\[
\int S_{\beta,\gamma}^2
w_k^\dagger\rho_\varepsilon\rho_\varepsilon
=J_x(k)+\frac{10}{\varepsilon^2}(\beta^2+\gamma^2)
\le J_{\max}(k,\varepsilon)
\]
whenever \((\beta,\gamma)=(\beta(q),\gamma(q))\).  Conditional on the coordinates and a fixed positive allocation count \(r=nq\), the directional Fisher information in the six arm--outcome cells is exactly
\[
I_{n,q}(x,h,\zeta)
=\alpha_n^2\sum_{a=1}^3
\frac{r_az_a(q)^2}
{1/4-\alpha_n^2(xv_a+hd_a^\dagger+\zeta)^2},
\]
and, if \(4\alpha_n^2L(k,\varepsilon)^2\le1/2\),
\[
I_{n,q}(x,h,\zeta)
\le\frac{4n\alpha_n^2/H(q)}
{1-4\alpha_n^2L(k,\varepsilon)^2}.
\]
The rational numbers \(C(k,\varepsilon)\), \(J_{\max}(k,\varepsilon)\), and
\(N(k,\varepsilon,\eta)\) are computable by finite exact arithmetic.  Every defining inequality for \(N(k,\varepsilon,\eta)\) holds for all \(n\ge N(k,\varepsilon,\eta)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The measures \(\lambda_v^\pm\), \(\lambda_d^\pm\), and
\(p_0^\dagger\) have total masses three, two, and one, respectively.  Therefore each of
\(s_x^\pm\), \(s_h^\pm\), and \(\gamma_0\) has total mass zero.  The central measure has
\(\sum_tp_{0,t}^\dagger b_t=0\).  The exact-primitives proposition gives
\[
\sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^+b_t=v,
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^-b_t=-v,
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^+b_t=d^\dagger,
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^-b_t=-d^\dagger.
\tag{1}
\]
Moreover,
\(b_{111}-b_{000}=\mathbf1\).  Substitution of the signed definitions into (1) proves the middle column of the table.  Since
\(\theta_t=(c^\dagger)^\top b_t\),
\((c^\dagger)^\top v=1\),
\((c^\dagger)^\top d^\dagger=0\), and
\((c^\dagger)^\top\mathbf1=0\), applying \((c^\dagger)^\top\) proves its last column.  Thus every displayed identity is exact.

For a noncentral response type the terms contributed by the appropriate
\(\lambda_v^\pm\) and \(\lambda_d^\pm\) are nonnegative, and
\(\gamma_0\) vanishes.  At either central type, the probability is bounded below by
\[
\frac12-\frac{\alpha_n}{2}(3|x|+2|h|)-\alpha_n|\zeta|
=\frac12\left[1-\alpha_n
\{3|x|+2|h|+2|\zeta|\}\right]\ge0,
\tag{2}
\]
because \(|x|\le T_k^\dagger\), \(|h|,|\zeta|\le\varepsilon\), and the stated positivity condition holds.  Zero total perturbation mass and (2) prove that the vector is a probability law.  Multiplying the table by \(x\), \(h\), and \(\zeta\) proves the two conditional-moment identities.  In particular the prior mean of the exact count target is \(\alpha_nx\); the target itself remains
\(n^{-1}\sum_tm_t\theta_t\) by the exact-primitives proposition.

Direct matrix multiplication gives
\[
\mathsf B^{-1}\mathsf B=I_3.
\tag{3}
\]
For positive \(q\), let
\[
\omega_a=\frac{(c_a^\dagger)^2}{q_aH(q)}.
\]
Then \(\omega_a\ge0\), \(\sum_a\omega_a=1\), and
\(z_a(q)=\omega_a/c_a^\dagger\).  It follows that
\[
(c^\dagger)^\top z(q)=\sum_a\omega_a=1,
\qquad
\sum_aq_az_a(q)^2
=\frac1{H(q)^2}\sum_a\frac{(c_a^\dagger)^2}{q_a}
=\frac1{H(q)}.
\tag{4}
\]
The last two rows of (3) give
\[
\beta(q)=-4\omega_2+\frac43\omega_3,
\qquad
\gamma(q)=\frac12\omega_1-\frac12\omega_2-
\frac12\omega_3=\omega_1-\frac12.
\tag{5}
\]
Because \(\omega\) is a probability vector, (5) gives
\(|\beta(q)|\le4\) and \(|\gamma(q)|\le1/2\).  At
\(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\), direct substitution gives
\(H(q^\dagger)=4\), \(z(q^\dagger)=v\), and hence
\(\beta(q^\dagger)=\gamma(q^\dagger)=0\).
By the definitions of \(J_x(k)\) and \(w_k^\dagger\),
\[
J_x(k)+\frac58\int|x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx
=\frac{4\int|(\varphi_k^\dagger)'|^2+
\kappa(c^\dagger)\int|x|(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2}
{\int(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2}.
\tag{6}
\]
The Airy-benchmark definition makes \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\) the minimum of this Rayleigh quotient, and the effective normalized Airy-record lemma bounds the right side of (6) above by
\(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+2^{-k}\).  This proves the asserted local saddle certificate and shows independently that the added face guards impose no score cost at
\(q^\dagger\).

If arm \(j\) is absent, set the arm-marginal direction equal to
\(e_j/c_j^\dagger\).  Its target derivative is one, while every observed coordinate has derivative zero.  Applying the explicit inverse in (3) yields, in order,
\[
\mathsf B^{-1}\frac{e_1}{c_1^\dagger}=(1,0,1/2)^\top,
\quad
\mathsf B^{-1}\frac{e_2}{c_2^\dagger}=(1,-4,-1/2)^\top,
\quad
\mathsf B^{-1}\frac{e_3}{c_3^\dagger}=(1,4/3,-1/2)^\top.
\tag{7}
\]
Every proper allocation face omits at least one arm, so (7) proves the face-guard assertion.  Notice that (7) is an infinitesimal score identity; it makes no claim that a finite path such as \(h=-4x\) remains inside the transverse box.

Write \(f=w_k^\dagger\rho_\varepsilon\rho_\varepsilon\).  On the interior of its support the directional prior score is
\[
S_{\beta,\gamma}
=\frac{(w_k^\dagger)'(x)}{w_k^\dagger(x)}
+\beta\frac{\rho_\varepsilon'(h)}{\rho_\varepsilon(h)}
+\gamma\frac{\rho_\varepsilon'(\zeta)}{\rho_\varepsilon(\zeta)}.
\tag{8}
\]
The compact spline square and the two polynomial densities vanish at their exterior boundaries.  Splitting at the finitely many spline breakpoints, ordinary one-dimensional integration by parts makes the internal boundary terms cancel by continuity and makes the exterior terms vanish.  Fubini's theorem therefore gives, for every continuously differentiable compact test function \(F\),
\[
\int D_{\beta,\gamma}F\,f
=-\int F S_{\beta,\gamma}f.
\tag{9}
\]
This proves the asserted directional identity without translating the rectangular support along a finite path.

Each one-dimensional score has mean zero.  Independence therefore kills all cross terms in the square of (7).  Since
\(w_k^\dagger=(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2/
\int(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2\), its score information is \(J_x(k)\).  Also,
\[
\frac{\rho_\varepsilon'(u)}{\rho_\varepsilon(u)}
=-\frac{4u}{\varepsilon^2-u^2},
\qquad
\int_{-\varepsilon}^{\varepsilon}
\left(\frac{\rho_\varepsilon'}{\rho_\varepsilon}\right)^2
\rho_\varepsilon
=\frac{15}{\varepsilon^5}
\int_{-\varepsilon}^{\varepsilon}u^2du
=\frac{10}{\varepsilon^2}.
\tag{10}
\]
Equations (5), (8), and (10) prove the score-information equality and the bound by
\(J_{\max}(k,\varepsilon)\).

Conditional on \((x,h,\zeta)\), the outcome in arm \(a\) is Bernoulli with success probability
\[
p_a=\frac12+\alpha_n(xv_a+hd_a^\dagger+\zeta).
\tag{11}
\]
In the parameter direction \((1,\beta(q),\gamma(q))\), its derivative is
\(\alpha_nz_a(q)\) by (3).  The Bernoulli Fisher-information identity and independence across labeled units give the exact displayed formula for
\(I_{n,q}\).  On the support, the absolute centered mean in (10) is at most
\(L(k,\varepsilon)\).  Hence
\[
\frac1{1/4-\alpha_n^2(xv_a+hd_a^\dagger+\zeta)^2}
\le\frac4{1-4\alpha_n^2L(k,\varepsilon)^2}.
\tag{12}
\]
Combining (4) and (12) proves the information upper bound.  For a boundary direction in (7), the derivative in every observed cell is zero, so its data information is exactly zero.

All entries in the two signed-direction arrays are rational.  The verified record gives exact rational spline integrals and an integer support radius.  Thus the maxima defining \(C(k,\varepsilon)\), as well as
\(J_{\max}(k,\varepsilon)\), are rational and computable by finite enumeration of the stated eight types and six cells.  Every left side in the definition of
\(N(k,\varepsilon,\eta)\) is nonincreasing in the integer argument and converges to zero.  Ordered-algebraic comparison decides each test, so sequential search terminates.  Monotonicity then proves that every accepted inequality remains true for every later \(n\).  This completes the proof.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the exact finite response-alphabet early-kill calculation required before any uniform Bayes expansion: the common-shift coordinate guards every proper allocation face and exposes the full directional score cost.
added_lemmas.gap: The lemma computes the tangent and information ledgers; it does not identify the Bayes risk of the random exact finite-population target with the Airy variational value.
added_lemmas.consumer: The face-robust orbit reduction, fixed-input evaluator, and open allocation-tube bridge use these identities.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Assume \(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\le1\).  Under the face-robust permutation-invariant prior
\(\nu_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\), every outcome-independent assignment law \(\mathcal D_n\) and every possibly randomized labeled-data estimator have Bayes risk at least
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi(r)
\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
\ge B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A},
\]
where \(\pi\) is the allocation-count law induced by \(\mathcal D_n\).  Conditional on a fixed allocation count, the posterior mean of the exact finite-population target attains the displayed fixed-count Bayes risk.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: After adding the independent common-shift coordinate, positivity requires \(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\le1\). The Bayes reduction itself is unchanged and is proved for the face-robust prior.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix integers \(n,k\ge1\), rationals \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\), and a verified spline record from
\(\mathrm{def:rational\text{-}airy\text{-}longitudinal\text{-}family}\).  If
\(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\le1\), finite-input mode of \(\mathsf E\) terminates.  It returns rationals \(b^-\le b^+\) with
\[
b^-\le B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\le b^+,
\qquad b^+-b^-\le\delta,
\qquad
R_n(c^\dagger)\ge B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\ge b^-.
\]
It also returns exact ordered-field maxima of
\(G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\) on the local, positive-count exterior, and zero-count sets in
\(\mathrm{def:evaluator\text{-}handle}\), and an exact rational feasible value \(U\) attained by a total procedure under the fixed independent design
\(q^\dagger\), so that \(R_n(c^\dagger)\le U\).  These are same-input finite certificates; no convergence in \(n\) is asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The finite evaluator must integrate the third coordinate and verify the stronger positivity inequality. It still makes only a same-input claim.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), there is one Turing machine extending \(\mathsf E\) with the following properties.  On input \(n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\), it uses the fixed-parameter diagonal in
\(\mathrm{def:evaluator\text{-}handle}\) and outputs an index \(k_n\), the complete verified spline record for \(\varphi_{k_n}^\dagger\), a rational
\(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}>0\), rational nonnegative errors
\(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\),
\(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), and \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\), and finite ordered-field certificates.  The outputs satisfy
\[
k_n\uparrow\infty,
\qquad \varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\downarrow0,
\qquad
\alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+4\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A})\le1.
\]
For
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_n&=\left\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a>0,
\ \left\|n^{1/6}(r/n-q^\dagger)\right\|_\infty
\le n^{1/72}\right\},\\
\mathcal X_n&=\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a>0\}
\setminus\mathcal L_n,\\
\mathcal Z_n&=\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a=0\},
\end{aligned}
\]
the certified all-count conclusions are
\[

added_lemmas.statement:
For every pair of integers \(n,k\geq1\) and every rational \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfying
\[
\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+2\varepsilon)\leq1,
\]
the legacy scalar Airy-tube deficit at the allocation count \((n,0,0)\) obeys
\[
G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A,0}(n,0,0)
\geq
\frac{11}{8}\int_{\mathbb R}|x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx
+\frac{45}{256}\varepsilon.
\]
Consequently, for every sequence \(k_n\to\infty\) and every sequence of positive rational numbers \(\varepsilon_n\) satisfying
\(\alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+2\varepsilon_n)\leq1\),
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n}^{\dagger,\mathrm A,0}(n,0,0)
\geq\frac{22}{15}\Lambda_{c^\dagger}
>\Lambda_{c^\dagger}.
\]
In particular, there is no sequence \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\to0\) for which
\[
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n}^{\dagger,\mathrm A,0}(r)
\leq\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{zero},n}
\]
holds for every allocation count \(r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}\) having at least one zero coordinate.  Thus the legacy scalar prior cannot furnish the zero-face part of a sharp all-count converse.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(n,k,\varepsilon\) satisfying the displayed admissibility condition.  Conditional on the scalar-tube coordinates \((x,h)\), the construction in \(\mathrm{def:scalar\text{-}airy\text{-}tube\text{-}legacy}\) first draws a count vector \(m\) from the multinomial law with cell probabilities \(p_{n,x,h,0}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\) and then draws a labeled response-type sequence uniformly in the orbit having counts \(m\).  If a labeled sequence \((t_1,\ldots,t_n)\) has counts \(m=(m_t)_t\), its conditional probability is
\[
\left\{\frac{n!}{\prod_t m_t!}
       \prod_t\bigl(p_{n,x,h,0,t}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\bigr)^{m_t}\right\}
\left\{\frac{\prod_t m_t!}{n!}\right\}
=\prod_{i=1}^n p_{n,x,h,0,t_i}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus, conditional on \((x,h)\), the labeled types are independent and identically distributed with that cell law.  By the scalar-legacy definition, this law is exactly the two-coordinate law in \(\mathrm{prop:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}exact\text{-}primitives}\).  The proposition and
\(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+2\varepsilon)\leq1\) therefore ensure that all eight probabilities are nonnegative and sum to one.

For the deterministic outcome-independent allocation having count vector \((n,0,0)\), all units are assigned to arm one, so the observed data reveal \(t_{i,1}\).  Define the observable estimator and its unit-level error by
\[
\widetilde\tau_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(2Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1),
\qquad
e(t)=2t_1-1-(c^\dagger)^\top t.
\tag{2}
\]
The exact finite-population target identity in
\(\mathrm{prop:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}exact\text{-}primitives}\) gives
\[
\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n e(t_i).
\tag{3}
\]
The same proposition gives \(v_1=1/2\), \(d_1^\dagger=0\),
\(\mathbb E[b_t\mid x,h]=\alpha_n(xv+hd^\dagger)\), and
\(\mathbb E[(c^\dagger)^\top t\mid x,h]=\alpha_nx\).  Since
\(2t_1-1=2(b_t)_1\), it follows that
\[
\mathbb E[e(t)\mid x,h]
=2\alpha_n(xv_1+hd_1^\dagger)-\alpha_nx=0.
\tag{4}
\]

For the lexicographically ordered types
\(000,001,010,011,100,101,110,111\), direct substitution of
\(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\) into (2) gives
\[
\bigl(e(t)^2\bigr)_t
=\left(1,\frac1{16},\frac9{16},0,0,
       \frac9{16},\frac1{16},1\right).
\tag{5}
\]
Because \(p_0^\dagger=(\delta_{000}+\delta_{111})/2\), equation (5) yields
\(\sum_t p_{0,t}^\dagger e(t)^2=1\).  Substitution into the four explicitly declared response measures gives, for either sign,
\[
\sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^{\pm}e(t)^2
=1+\frac9{16}+\frac1{16}=\frac{13}{8},
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^{\pm}e(t)^2
=\frac{23}{16}.
\tag{6}
\]
The longitudinal measures have mass three and the transverse measures have mass two.  The scalar fiber is
\[
p_{n,x,h,0,t}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
=p_{0,t}^\dagger+\alpha_n\left\{
|x|\lambda_{v,t}^{\operatorname{sign}(x)}
+|h|\lambda_{d,t}^{\operatorname{sign}(h)}
-(3|x|+2|h|)p_{0,t}^\dagger\right\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Combining (5)--(7) proves the exact conditional second-moment identity
\[
\mathbb E[e(t)^2\mid x,h]
=1-\alpha_n\left(\frac{11}{8}|x|+
                         \frac9{16}|h|\right).
\tag{8}
\]

By the conditional independence in (1), the zero conditional mean in (4), and (3),
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[
(\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_{c^\dagger}(m))^2\mid x,h\right]
=\frac1n\left\{1-\alpha_n\left(
\frac{11}{8}|x|+\frac9{16}|h|\right)\right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
The coordinates are independent under the legacy prior, with respective densities
\(w_k^\dagger\) and \(\rho_\varepsilon\).  From the declared polynomial formula for the latter,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_{\mathbb R}|h|\rho_\varepsilon(h)\,dh
&=\frac{30}{16\varepsilon}\int_0^\varepsilon
h\left(1-\frac{h^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right)^2dh\\
&=\frac{30\varepsilon}{16}\int_0^1u(1-u^2)^2du
=\frac5{16}\varepsilon.
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
Since \(\alpha_n=n^{-1/3}\), averaging (9) and applying (10) shows that the Bayes risk of the particular estimator \(\widetilde\tau_n\) is
\[
\frac1n-n^{-4/3}\left\{
\frac{11}{8}\int_{\mathbb R}|x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx
+\frac{45}{256}\varepsilon\right\}.
\tag{11}
\]
Under squared error, for every observation value with positive prior-predictive probability, completing the square shows that the conditional posterior mean uniquely minimizes conditional risk; observation values of zero prior-predictive probability contribute zero.  Hence the exact posterior-mean risk
\(\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A,0}(n,0,0)\) in
\(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}scalar\text{-}airy\text{-}tube\text{-}bayes\text{-}risk}\) is at most (11).  The definition
\[
G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A,0}(r)
=n^{4/3}\left\{n^{-1}-
\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A,0}(r)\right\}
\tag{12}
\]
then proves the first asserted inequality, including the positive transverse term.

It remains to calculate the limit of the longitudinal term.  Put
\(\Phi=\phi_{c^\dagger}\),
\(A=\int_{\mathbb R}|\Phi'(x)|^2dx\), and
\(B=\int_{\mathbb R}|x|\Phi(x)^2dx\).  Both integrals are finite by
\(\mathrm{def:airy\text{-}benchmark}\).  For \(s>0\), the function
\(\Phi_s(x)=s^{1/2}\Phi(sx)\) has unit \(L^2\) norm, and a change of variables gives its Airy energy as
\[
E(s)=4s^2A+\kappa(c^\dagger)s^{-1}B.
\tag{13}
\]
The ground-state variational property in
\(\mathrm{def:airy\text{-}benchmark}\) makes \(s=1\) a minimum of the differentiable function (13).  Therefore
\[
0=E'(1)=8A-\kappa(c^\dagger)B.
\tag{14}
\]
Together with
\(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=4A+\kappa(c^\dagger)B\), equation (14) yields
\[
B=\frac{2\Lambda_{c^\dagger}}
        {3\kappa(c^\dagger)}
=\frac{16}{15}\Lambda_{c^\dagger},
\tag{15}
\]
where the last equality uses
\(\kappa(c^\dagger)=5/8\) from
\(\mathrm{prop:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}exact\text{-}primitives}\).

By \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}normalized\text{-}airy\text{-}record}\),
\(\varphi_k^\dagger\to\Phi\) in weighted \(H^1\).  In particular,
\(\int(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2\to1\), and Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_{\mathbb R}|x|
\left|(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2-\Phi^2\right|dx
&\leq
\left(\int_{\mathbb R}|x|
|\varphi_k^\dagger-\Phi|^2dx\right)^{1/2}\\
&\quad\times
\left(\int_{\mathbb R}|x|
|\varphi_k^\dagger+\Phi|^2dx\right)^{1/2}
\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{16}
\]
The second factor is bounded because weighted \(L^2\) convergence and the finiteness of \(B\) bound it.  Since
\(w_k^\dagger=(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2/
\int(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2\), equations (15)--(16) imply
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}|x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx
\longrightarrow\frac{16}{15}\Lambda_{c^\dagger}.
\tag{17}
\]
For any admissible sequences in the statement, the transverse summand in the first inequality is nonnegative.  Taking the lower limit and using (17) gives
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n}^{\dagger,\mathrm A,0}(n,0,0)
\geq\frac{11}{8}\frac{16}{15}\Lambda_{c^\dagger}
=\frac{22}{15}\Lambda_{c^\dagger}.
\tag{18}
\]
The benchmark definition and \(\kappa(c^\dagger)=5/8>0\) give
\(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}>0\), so the last member of (18) is strictly larger than \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\).  Finally, \((n,0,0)\) has zero coordinates.  If the asserted uniform sequence \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\to0\) existed, its bound at \((n,0,0)\) would imply a lower limit no greater than \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\), contradicting (18).  This proves the final assertion.
